title: Test day: what to expect
lines: Test day is not the time for surprises. Most of what goes wrong on the day has nothing to do with knowledge: a late arrival, an ID problem, a noisy room or a computer that fails the system check. This article walks through the day for both test center and at-home candidates. Rules can change, so read the current requirements on ets.org a week before your test and again the day before.
## The week before
- Take your last full mock test four to six days before the exam, at the same time of day as your real test.
- Read the ID requirements on ets.org and check that the name on your ID matches your registration exactly, including the order of names and any middle name.
- Plan your route to the test center, or prepare your room and computer for an at-home test.
- Keep your sleep regular. Two nights of good sleep before the test matter more than one extra evening of study.
## Your ID

You will need valid, acceptable identification, usually an original government-issued photo ID such as a passport. Photocopies and expired documents are normally refused. If your ID is not accepted, you may not be allowed to test and may lose your fee. Check the exact rules for your country on ets.org well in advance; this is one of the most common, and most avoidable, problems.
## At a test center
- Arrive early: aim for at least 30 minutes before your appointment. Late arrivals may be turned away.
- Check-in usually includes showing your ID, a photo, signing a confidentiality statement and storing your belongings in a locker. Phones, watches, notes and food are not allowed in the testing room.
- Staff give you scratch paper and pencils for notes. You may be able to ask for more during the test; ask the center how it works.
- You may wear earplugs or headphones provided by the center if available, since other candidates may be taking different tests around you.
## At home
- Run the ETS system check on the exact computer, network and room you will use, a few days before and again on the day.
- Use a desktop or laptop (not a tablet), with a webcam, microphone and speaker. Close every other program.
- Choose a quiet, private room with a clear desk. A proctor will ask you to show the room with your camera.

- Note-taking at home is limited to approved materials, such as a small whiteboard with an erasable marker or a transparent sheet with an erasable marker. Paper is not allowed. Check ets.org for the current list, and erase your notes in front of the proctor at the end.
- Start the check-in process early. Connecting with the proctor and showing your room can take some time.
! Practice with the same note-taking tool you will use on test day. Writing on a small whiteboard is slower than on paper, so get used to it during your mock tests.
## During the test
The test opens with the 30-minute essay, then moves through the four Verbal and Quant sections. There is no scheduled break between sections. Plan for close to two hours of continuous focus.
- Use the restroom just before you start.
- Eat a normal meal one to two hours before the test, so you are neither hungry nor sleepy.
- Drink some water before, but not so much that you need to leave the room.
- If you must take an unscheduled break, the clock keeps running, and at-home rules are strict. Ask about the current rules in advance.
## Handling problems in the room

If something goes wrong, such as a frozen screen, a noise that will not stop or a calculator that does not respond, raise your hand at a center or contact the proctor through the chat at home. Report it right away, not after the test is over. Stay calm: a short pause to fix a problem is better than an hour of distraction.
## Mindset on the day
- Expect at least one question that seems impossible. Every test taker meets some. Mark it, guess and move on.
- Do not try to judge from section 2 whether you did well in section 1. It wastes attention.
- Between sections, take one slow breath, reset your posture and read the next section's first question fresh.
## After the test

At the end you will see your unofficial Verbal and Quant scores. Your official scores, with the essay score, arrive later. If you are unhappy with your result, do not decide anything that day. Rest, then read the article on retakes and use your score report to plan.
## Rehearse with the app

Take at least two of this app's mock tests as full rehearsals: same start time as your real test, phone away, no breaks, essay included, and the same note-taking tool. A rehearsal makes the real day feel familiar.
